In the last ten years, I have bought a few pieces of guitar/music equipment, and I found the best thing to do was using search engine to find the best deal after deciding specifically what I wanted. I was able to save hundreds doing this. It worked out great for electronic things that are intended to be perfectly uniform such as amps, pedals, and a recorder. For some reason there was a music store out there selling the one thing I wanted cheaper than anywhere else. When I checked their prices on other things, they were nowhere near cheapest. Of course there is a small risk of getting scammed or suffering with bad customer service when buying from random music stores all over the country. You also have to pay for shipping if you want to do a return.

On the other hand, I ended up choosing a seven-string guitar once and I ordered it online. I did end up saving about $200 on it, but it ended up where I had to admit that I simply didn't like how it sounded, especially how it sounded going into my amp. I found a video of a famous guitarist playing something on the same model of guitar, and it had the same kind of tone. Well, I ended up selling it, because I needed the money anyway. So if you're buying a guitar, I recommend that you buy it from a music store where you can listen to it, and preferably, plug it into the same amp that you're going to use. This is especially true for acoustic guitars, which I find can have a different tone to them even if they're the same model. My brother and I both had the same model of acoustic guitar by Fender. For some reason mine always sounded better than his. They had a different external appearance, but it was built with the same design and internal materials. I recommend always getting an acoustic guitar from a store where you can play it first. If you're an intermediate level musician, you should already be a tone fanatic, and since the very beginning, I've always preferred guitars that feel comfortable. I might tolerate a guitar that sounds great and feels terrible for a recording, but it's something you should avoid as it will discourage you from playing and especially practicing.
